name: Aruba
prevalence_note: The Centrale Bank van Aruba (CBA) has issued public warnings about websites that impersonate a financial supervisor for Aruba or a former Aruban commercial bank, and about a lookalike domain used to collect personal data from people who already think they have been defrauded and to push them to call numbers beginning with +284, an area code the Bank links to one-ring fraud.
cross_border_note: Legitimate Aruban authorities and the CBA use the +297 country code. The Bank specifically warned that the lookalike supervisor site used +284 numbers and even borrowed a visiting address that belongs to another Aruban institution. The British Virgin Islands Financial Services Commission and IOSCO also published alerts on the fake Aruba Financial Services Commission site.

scams.name: Lookalike site posing as Aruba's financial supervisor, with +284 call-back
scams.name_en: CBA 20 October 2023 warning: a fraudulent site designed to look like Aruba's financial supervisor collects names, addresses and emails, especially from earlier fraud victims, and steers them to telephone numbers starting with +284, which the Bank links to one-ring fraud
context_keywords: website that mimics the Aruban supervisor
asks for name, address and email after a fraud
uses an address that belongs to another Oranjestad body

red_flag_keywords.text: enter your details so the Aruban supervisor can help
call this +284 number about your case
site that looks like the central bank but is not cbaruba.org
one-ring call that asks you to ring back

scams.signals_en: On 20 Oct 2023 the CBA warned of a fake Aruban financial-supervisor site stealing emails, names and addresses (often from past fraud victims) or pushing +284 one-ring callbacks instead of +297, copying CBA/FIU domains and wrong addresses.
scams.legit_en: The Centrale Bank van Aruba's real site is its own published domain, and genuine Aruban official numbers use +297. Neither the CBA nor the FIU collects victim details via a lookalike site or asks for +284 callbacks.
bait_tactics: Do not enter a name, address or email on a site that only resembles the CBA or the FIU, and do not call back a +284 number from that page.
Check the address against the Bank's published domain, and raise any doubt through a contact route found on that official site, not through the lookalike page.

If details may already have been entered, tell the customer's own bank or card issuer, change passwords, watch the statements, and say the site can be reported to the police or the public prosecutor, as the CBA advises.

scams.name: Fake financial services commission and former-bank site used for investments or refunds
scams.name_en: CBA public warning: two fraudulent websites, one posing as a single financial-services regulator for Aruba and one posing as a former commercial bank, which the Bank has reason to believe are linked; people were told to open an account in order to invest or to receive a reimbursement, and some lost significant sums
context_keywords: self-described financial services commission for Aruba
website reusing the name of a former Aruban bank
open an account to invest or to get a refund
uses the central bank's published contact details

red_flag_keywords.text: open an account here to invest or to get a reimbursement
we are the only financial regulator in Aruba
enter personal data on this unofficial bank site
securities or derivatives sold from an unknown page

scams.signals_en: CBA warned of two linked scam sites: a fake Aruba Financial Services Commission copying CBA's address/numbers (also flagged by BVI FSC and IOSCO) and a fake former commercial bank urging victims to open accounts to invest or claim refunds.
scams.legit_en: Centrale Bank van Aruba is the supervisor; a former bank name or copied CBA contacts on a new site do not make it licensed. Genuine refund or investment accounts open only with firms verified via official Aruban channels.
bait_tactics: Refuse to open an account or to send money for an investment or a reimbursement on a site that is not the customer's known bank or the CBA.
Treat copied official contact details or the recycled name of a former bank as a warning sign, not as proof.
If money or data may already have been given, contact the real bank or card issuer, change passwords, watch the statements, and report the sites to the police or the public prosecutor.
